{"replaced": "the term ideal machine refers to a hypothetical mechanical system in which energy and power are not lost or dissipated through friction , deformation , wear , or other inefficiencies . ideal machines have the theoretical maximum performance , and therefore are used as a baseline for evaluating the performance of real mechanical systems . a simple machine , such as a screw , camshaft , or gear train , is \" ideal \" if the power input is equal to the power output of the ===machine=== , which means there are no faults . in this case , the machine efficiency is 100 % . mechanical efficiency is the performance of the machine compared to its theoretical lifetime as performed by an ideal machine . the mechanical efficiency of a simple machine is calculated by dividing the actual power input by the actual power output . this is normally expressed as a percentage . energy loss in a mechanical machine can occur in many ways , such as through friction , deformation , wear , mechanical losses , and chemical conversion , mechanical and electrical losses .", "replaced_ids": [86, 86], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "the axe bow is a wave - piercing type of a ship ' s bow , characterised by a vertical stem and a relatively long and narrow entry ( front hull ) . the bow stem is straight and the freeboard is low , with little flare , so that the overall shape resembles an axe . the bow cuts through the water , and is less affected by cutting through waves than a bow with more stem , making this bow type much less prone to flooding . because the forward bow stem does not always rise above the water level , it is less prone to slamming . the axe bow shifts the center of sail area forwards and the ship may require even more rudder control to keep its height , and this increases with the increased sail area . a vertical bow stem is not unique ; they were common in the early shipbuilding era . the ===design=== of the axe bow is associated with a vertical bow stem of the ship . this concept was developed in the 1950s by janus van gogh of delft university of technology , the royal netherlands navy institute , marin ( maritime research institute netherlands ) , the royal netherlands sea research institution , the british admiralty shipyard , the dutch navy , british naval shipbuilding and the norwegian national home shipbuilding .", "replaced_ids": [161, 161], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "in cognitive psychology , brown \u2013 peterson task ( or brown \u2013 peterson procedure ) refers to a cognitive exercise purposed for testing the limits of working memory capacity . the task is named for two similar experiments published in the 1950s in which it was first developed , the first by donald brown and the second by husband and wife , donald and martha peterson . the task aims to assess the number of items that can be kept in working memory while preventing participants from using the computer program or other memory resources separate from the working memory to increase memory capacity . in the task , participants ===choose=== a pair of three - dimensional objects , or three squares pairs , and are instructed to perform complex algebraic operations , such as counting backwards by 1 down from 1 between each two squares . a trigram consists of 3 non - morphemic letters , the importance of which is that each letter represents a mentally independent unit to be kept in working memory ; therefore , trigrams are letter combinations that represent words or common acronyms . the same computations are administered between the two objects to show the participant isn ' t using mnemonic devices to merge the pairs into a single object . variants of the brown \u2013 * task are still used today , all with the same basic principles of providing items for the participant to recall whilst avoiding the usage of other cognitive resources to help maintain working memory .", "replaced_ids": [110, 110], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "the axe bow is a wave - piercing type of a ship ' s bow , characterised by a vertical stem and a relatively long and narrow entry ( front hull ) . the bow stem is straight and the freeboard is low , with little flare , so that the overall shape resembles an axe . the bow cuts through the water , and is less affected by cutting through waves than a bow with more stem , making this bow type much less prone to flooding . because the forward bow stem does not always rise above the water level , it is less prone to slamming . the axe bow shifts the center of sail area forwards and the ship may require even more rudder control to keep its height , and this increases with the increased sail area . a vertical bow stem is not unique ; they were common in the early shipbuilding era . the design of the axe bow is associated with a vertical bow stem of the ship . this concept was developed in the 1950s by janus van gogh of delft university of technology , the royal netherlands navy institute , marin ( maritime research institute netherlands ) , the royal netherlands sea ===research=== institution , the british admiralty shipyard , the dutch navy , british naval shipbuilding and the norwegian national home shipbuilding .", "replaced_ids": [212, 212], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "in cognitive psychology , brown \u2013 peterson task ( or brown \u2013 peterson procedure ) refers to a cognitive exercise purposed for testing the limits of working memory capacity . the task is named for two similar experiments published in the 1950s in which it was first developed , the first by donald brown and the second by husband and wife , donald and martha peterson . the task aims to assess the number of items that can be kept in working memory while preventing participants from using the computer program or other memory ===resources=== separate from the working memory to increase memory capacity . in the task , participants choose a pair of three - dimensional objects , or three squares pairs , and are instructed to perform complex algebraic operations , such as counting backwards by 1 down from 1 between each two squares . a trigram consists of 3 non - morphemic letters , the importance of which is that each letter represents a mentally independent unit to be kept in working memory ; therefore , trigrams are letter combinations that represent words or common acronyms . the same computations are administered between the two objects to show the participant isn ' t using mnemonic devices to merge the pairs into a single object . variants of the brown \u2013 * task are still used today , all with the same basic principles of providing items for the participant to recall whilst avoiding the usage of other cognitive resources to help maintain working memory .", "replaced_ids": [94, 94], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "the axe bow is a wave - piercing type of a ship ' s bow , characterised by a vertical stem and a relatively long and narrow entry ( front hull ) . the bow stem is straight and the freeboard is low , with little flare , so that the overall shape resembles an axe . the bow cuts through the water , and is less affected by cutting through waves than a bow with more stem , making this bow type much less prone to flooding . because the forward bow stem does not always rise above the water level , it is less prone to slamming . the axe bow shifts the center of sail area forwards and the ship may require even more rudder control to keep its height , and this increases with the increased sail area . a vertical bow stem is not unique ; they were common in the early shipbuilding era . the design of the axe bow is ===associated=== with a vertical bow stem of the ship . this concept was developed in the 1950s by janus van gogh of delft university of technology , the royal netherlands navy institute , marin ( maritime research institute netherlands ) , the royal netherlands sea research institution , the british admiralty shipyard , the dutch navy , british naval shipbuilding and the norwegian national home shipbuilding .", "replaced_ids": [167, 167], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "the axe bow is a wave - piercing type of a ship ' s bow , characterised by a vertical stem and a relatively long and narrow entry ( front hull ) . the bow stem is straight and the freeboard is low , with little flare , so that the overall shape resembles an axe . the bow cuts through the water , and is less affected by cutting through waves than a bow with more stem , making this bow type much less prone to ===flooding=== . because the forward bow stem does not always rise above the water level , it is less prone to slamming . the axe bow shifts the center of sail area forwards and the ship may require even more rudder control to keep its height , and this increases with the increased sail area . a vertical bow stem is not unique ; they were common in the early shipbuilding era . the design of the axe bow is associated with a vertical bow stem of the ship . this concept was developed in the 1950s by janus van gogh of delft university of technology , the royal netherlands navy institute , marin ( maritime research institute netherlands ) , the royal netherlands sea research institution , the british admiralty shipyard , the dutch navy , british naval shipbuilding and the norwegian national home shipbuilding .", "replaced_ids": [87, 87], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "in cognitive psychology , brown \u2013 peterson task ( or brown \u2013 peterson procedure ) refers to a cognitive exercise purposed for testing the limits of working memory capacity . the task is named for two similar experiments published in the 1950s in which it was first developed , the first by donald brown and the second by husband and wife , donald and martha peterson . the task aims to assess the number of items that can be kept in working memory while preventing participants from using ===the computer program=== or other memory resources separate from the working memory to increase memory capacity . in the task , participants choose a pair of three - dimensional objects , or three squares pairs , and are instructed to perform complex algebraic operations , such as counting backwards by 1 down from 1 between each two squares . a trigram consists of 3 non - morphemic letters , the importance of which is that each letter represents a mentally independent unit to be kept in working memory ; therefore , trigrams are letter combinations that represent words or common acronyms . the same computations are administered between the two objects to show the participant isn ' t using mnemonic devices to merge the pairs into a single object . variants of the brown \u2013 * task are still used today , all with the same basic principles of providing items for the participant to recall whilst avoiding the usage of other cognitive resources to help maintain working memory .", "replaced_ids": [88, 90], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "the axe bow is a wave - piercing type of a ship ' s bow , characterised by a vertical stem and a relatively long and narrow entry ( front hull ) . the bow stem is straight and the freeboard is low , with little flare , so that the overall shape resembles an axe . the bow cuts through the water , and is less affected by cutting through waves than a bow with more ===stem=== , making this bow type much less prone to flooding . because the forward bow stem does not always rise above the water level , it is less prone to slamming . the axe bow shifts the center of sail area forwards and the ship may require even more rudder control to keep its height , and this increases with the increased sail area . a vertical bow stem is not unique ; they were common in the early shipbuilding era . the design of the axe bow is associated with a vertical bow stem of the ship . this concept was developed in the 1950s by janus van gogh of delft university of technology , the royal netherlands navy institute , marin ( maritime research institute netherlands ) , the royal netherlands sea research institution , the british admiralty shipyard , the dutch navy , british naval shipbuilding and the norwegian national home shipbuilding .", "replaced_ids": [77, 77], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "the existence of ko fights is implied by the rule of ko , a special rule of the game that prevents immediate repetition of position , by a short ' loop ' in which a single stone is captured , and another single stone immediately taken back . the rule specifies that the first recapture is forbidden , for one turn only . this gives rise to the following situation : the ' banned ' player makes a bid , which may have no particular good effect , but which causes an effective reply . then the game has come to its end , and recapture is forbidden . this form of game play is termed a ko threat . if white , say , chooses to make a ko threat , and black responds to the threat instead of ending the game in some way , then white can recapture the player that ===makes=== the ko . this leaves black in the same position that white was formerly in : black can choose to give up the ko , or to find a ko threat . if black and white alternate making the threats with both making up the ko , they are having a ko fight .", "replaced_ids": [154, 154], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "agenda setting occurs through a cognitive process known as \" accessibility \" . this implies that the more frequently and prominently the news media discusses an issue , the more instances of that issue become present in one ' s mind . when people are asked what the most important issue in the news is , they respond with the most accessible news issue in question , which is typically the issue the news is focused on the most . the agenda - setting effect is not the result of receiving one or a few messages but is due to the collective impact of a very large number of media , each of which has a specific topic but all of which deal with the same major issue . mass - media coverage in general and agenda - setting in particular also has a powerful effect on what people think that other people are thinking , and hence they tend to allocate more attention to issues that have been recently covered by the media . this is also called schemata effect . in linguistic and cognitive psychology , a schema ( plural , concepts , or schemas ) is a ===category=== of information or behavior that describes pieces of information and the relationships among them .", "replaced_ids": [200, 200], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "a symbolic analysis of relay and switching circuits is the title of a master ' s thesis written by computer science pioneer claude e . shannon while attending the massachusetts institute of technology ( mit ) in 1937 . in his thesis , shannon , a law degree graduate of john s . harvard , showed that boolean algebra could be used to precisely describe the behaviour of the electrical switches that were the building block of the electrical network of the american telephone system of america monopoly . he went on to prove that it should also be possible to use arrangements of relays to solve linear linear algebra problems . the analysis of the binary representation of electrical switches to perform logic functions is the basic idea that today defines all current digital circuit designs . shannon ' s paper became the basis of practical digital circuit design when it became widely accepted among the electrical engineering community during and after the 20th century . at the time , the techniques employed to design digital circuits were ad hoc in nature and superseded the formal techniques that shannon ' s paper supplied to computer projects . charles howard gardner regarded shannon ' s thesis as \" possibly the most valuable , and also the most influential , master ' s thesis of all time \" . a summary of the work was published in the 1938 ===volume=== of the transactions of the american institute of electrical engineers , and in 1955 , it earned shannon the alfred noble american institute of american engineers award .", "replaced_ids": [238, 238], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "the axe bow is a wave - piercing type of a ship ' s bow , characterised by a vertical stem and a relatively long and narrow entry ( front hull ) . the bow stem is straight and the freeboard is low , with little flare , so that the overall shape resembles an axe . the bow cuts through the water , and is less affected by cutting through waves than a bow with more stem , making this bow type much less prone to flooding . because the forward bow stem does not always rise above the water level , it is less prone to slamming . the axe bow shifts the center of sail area forwards and the ship may require even more rudder control to ===keep=== its height , and this increases with the increased sail area . a vertical bow stem is not unique ; they were common in the early shipbuilding era . the design of the axe bow is associated with a vertical bow stem of the ship . this concept was developed in the 1950s by janus van gogh of delft university of technology , the royal netherlands navy institute , marin ( maritime research institute netherlands ) , the royal netherlands sea research institution , the british admiralty shipyard , the dutch navy , british naval shipbuilding and the norwegian national home shipbuilding .", "replaced_ids": [130, 130], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "agenda setting occurs through a cognitive process known as \" accessibility \" . this implies that the more frequently and prominently the news media discusses an issue , the more instances of that issue become present in one ' s mind . when people are asked what the most important issue in the news is , they respond with the most accessible news issue in question , which is typically the issue the news is focused on the most . the agenda - setting effect is not the result of receiving one or a few messages but is due to the collective impact of a very large number of media , each of which has a specific topic but all of which deal with the same major issue . mass - media coverage in general and agenda - setting in particular also has a powerful effect on what ===people=== think that other people are thinking , and hence they tend to allocate more attention to issues that have been recently covered by the media . this is also called schemata effect . in linguistic and cognitive psychology , a schema ( plural , concepts , or schemas ) is a category of information or behavior that describes pieces of information and the relationships among them .", "replaced_ids": [148, 148], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "agenda setting occurs through a cognitive process known as \" accessibility \" . this implies that the more frequently and prominently the news media discusses an issue , the more instances of that issue become present in one ' s mind . when people are asked what the most important issue in the news is , they respond with the most accessible news issue in question , which is typically the issue the news is focused on the most . the agenda - setting effect is not the result of receiving one or a few messages but is due to the collective impact of a very large number of media , each of which has a specific topic but all of which deal with the same major issue . mass - media coverage in general and agenda - setting in particular also has a powerful effect on what people think that other people are thinking , and hence they tend to allocate more attention to issues that have been recently covered by the media . this is also called schemata effect . in linguistic and cognitive psychology , a schema ( plural , concepts , or schemas ) ===is=== a category of information or behavior that describes pieces of information and the relationships among them .", "replaced_ids": [198, 198], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "in macroeconomics and international finance , the capital account is one of two primary components of the balance of payments , the other being the current account . whereas the current account represents a nation ' s real income , the capital account represents net change in ownership of national assets . a surplus in the capital account means money is flowing into the country , but unlike a surplus in the current account , the money that flows can be income , or sale of assets rather than money for work . a deficit in the capital account means money is flowing out of the country , and it ===means=== the country is losing its ownership of its assets . the term \" capital account \" is used with a narrower meaning by the international monetary fund ( imf ) and affiliated institutions . the imf splits what the rest of the world calls the current account into two top - level components : financial account and monetary account , with by far the majority of the transactions being recorded in its financial records .", "replaced_ids": [110, 110], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "in cognitive psychology , brown \u2013 peterson task ( or brown \u2013 peterson procedure ) refers to a cognitive exercise purposed for testing the limits of working memory capacity . the task is named for two similar experiments published in the 1950s in which it was first developed , the first by donald brown and the second by husband and wife , donald and martha peterson . the task aims to assess the number of items that can be kept in working memory while preventing participants from using the computer program or other memory resources separate from the working memory to increase memory capacity . in the task , participants choose a pair of three - dimensional objects , or three squares pairs , and are instructed to perform complex algebraic operations , such as counting backwards by 1 down from 1 between each two squares . a trigram consists of 3 non - morphemic letters , the importance of which is that each letter represents a mentally independent unit to be ===kept=== in working memory ; therefore , trigrams are letter combinations that represent words or common acronyms . the same computations are administered between the two objects to show the participant isn ' t using mnemonic devices to merge the pairs into a single object . variants of the brown \u2013 * task are still used today , all with the same basic principles of providing items for the participant to recall whilst avoiding the usage of other cognitive resources to help maintain working memory .", "replaced_ids": [172, 172], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "the axe bow is a wave - piercing type of a ship ' s bow , characterised by a vertical stem and a relatively long and narrow entry ( front hull ) . the bow stem is straight and the freeboard is low , with little flare , so that the overall shape resembles an axe . the bow cuts through the water , and is less affected by ===cutting=== through waves than a bow with more stem , making this bow type much less prone to flooding . because the forward bow stem does not always rise above the water level , it is less prone to slamming . the axe bow shifts the center of sail area forwards and the ship may require even more rudder control to keep its height , and this increases with the increased sail area . a vertical bow stem is not unique ; they were common in the early shipbuilding era . the design of the axe bow is associated with a vertical bow stem of the ship . this concept was developed in the 1950s by janus van gogh of delft university of technology , the royal netherlands navy institute , marin ( maritime research institute netherlands ) , the royal netherlands sea research institution , the british admiralty shipyard , the dutch navy , british naval shipbuilding and the norwegian national home shipbuilding .", "replaced_ids": [69, 69], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "in cognitive psychology , brown \u2013 peterson task ( or brown \u2013 peterson procedure ) refers to a cognitive exercise purposed for testing the limits of working memory capacity . the task is named for two similar experiments published in the 1950s in which it was first developed , the first by donald brown and the second by husband and wife , donald and martha peterson . the task aims to assess the number of items that can be kept in working memory while preventing participants from using the computer program or other memory resources separate from the working memory to increase memory capacity . in the task , participants choose a pair of three - dimensional objects , or three squares pairs , and are instructed to perform complex algebraic operations , such as counting backwards by 1 down from 1 between each two squares . a trigram consists of 3 non - morphemic letters , the importance of which is that each letter represents a mentally independent unit to be kept in working memory ; therefore , trigrams are letter combinations that represent words or common acronyms . the same computations are administered between the two objects to ===show=== the participant isn ' t using mnemonic devices to merge the pairs into a single object . variants of the brown \u2013 * task are still used today , all with the same basic principles of providing items for the participant to recall whilst avoiding the usage of other cognitive resources to help maintain working memory .", "replaced_ids": [200, 200], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "soil ph is a measure of the acidity or basicity ( alkalinity ) of a soil . it is defined as the inverse ( inverse ) value ( < 1 ) of the concentration of hydronium ion ( ho\u2212 or , more precisely , h \u2083o\u207a aq ) in a solution . in soils , it is measured in a 1 liter measure of soil mixed with water ( or a salt solution , such as 0 . 01 m cacl \u2082 ) , and typically falls between 3 and 10 , with most being neutral . acidic soils have a ph below 7 and most neutral acid soils have a ph above 9 . ultra - acidic soils ( ph below 8 . 2 ) and very - acid acidified soils ( ph below 7 ) are rare . soil ph is considered a master variable in soils as it affects many biological processes . it also affects soil nutrient availability by determining the relative forms of the soil , and thus the chemical reactions they perform . the optimum ph range for most plants is approximately 1 % ( 100 % ) acid ; however , many species have adapted to ===grow=== at phes outside this range .", "replaced_ids": [203, 203], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "putlog holes or putlock holes are small holes made in the walls of structures to receive the ends of poles ( small round logs ) or beams , called putlogs or putlocks , to support a scaffolding . putlog holes may extend through a wall to provide access on both sides of the wall . a once common form of scaffolding , putlog holes ===derive=== from ancient roman construction . the name putlock and the english term putlog date from the renaissance , and are still used today . the poles themselves may be supported on the outer ends by vertical poles ( ribs ) , cantilevered by one end being permanently fixed in the wall , or be used alternatively by penetrating the wall to support the vertical poles supported on both sides . the poles themselves may be closed - off flush with the wall if they cannot be accessed , but the remaining open holes are often filled in as the scaffold is used to prevent water from reaching the ground . some natural holes themselves may be left open , particularly if not in a confined space . the original designs ' large overall volume and the depthiness of the holes ensure that they did not affect the solidity of the building , and in well - preserved castles , like beaumaris , the ancient putlog holes can be seen to this day .", "replaced_ids": [64, 64], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "a portable engine is an engine , either a steam engine or an internal combustion engine , that sits in one place while operating ( providing power to machinery ) , but ( unlike a stationary engine ) is portable and thus can be easily moved from one work site to another . mounted on wheels or other equipment , it is either towed to the work site or moves there via self - propulsion . portable engines were in common use in industrialised countries from the earliest days of steam engine use , during an era when electric power generation was widespread . before that , most power generation and transmission were by animal , horse , machine , or human ; after that , a period of electrification ( including locomotive electrification ) and large machinery and vehicles ( such as buses , trucks , cars , engine - cars , and locomotives with their wheels turned in ) limited most use of portable engines . in developing countries today , portable engines still have some use ( particularly in the form of modern diesel engines mounted on boards ) , although the technologies listed above increasingly lose their use there as well . in industrialised countries they are no longer used for production processes , but preserved examples can often be seen at steam fairs driving appropriate locomotives for demonstration purposes . portable engines during their era usually were either towed to their work sites by draft animals or oxen , or , in the latter part of that era , by power including self - propulsion or towing by traction engines , steam engines , other tractors , or trucks . they were used to power agricultural machinery ( such as in farming machine shops ) , milling ===machines=== ( such as in mill equipment shops , steel mills , and ore mines ) , pumps and fans ( such as in mines and oil wells ) , and in mine shafts ( for power pumps , power toolsets , presses , and other machines ) .", "replaced_ids": [302, 302], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "the banshee ( 1925 ) is a string piano composition by american composer and music theorist henry cowell ( 1897 \u2013 1965 ) . it was the first piano piece composed to be performed completely free of the keyboard , using only the vibration of the strings within the instrument to produce sound . cowell wrote that his inspiration in developing the \" new string piano \" system of playing stemmed from a determination to change \" the nature of piano \" , finding new techniques in and adapting for other instruments without necessarily inventing new ones . in addition to the new piano system allowing the smoother of producing sounds , composition of the \" instrument \" also required the performer to play the instrument in a particular orientation , standing in the crook of the arm closest to the keyboard , rather than seated at a bench . this process of re - positioning was an intentional element of the piece , as conservatory - trained performers would re - assume the posture of a new student , forced to quickly pick out the notes on the keyboard to determine their sound . due to this unusual style , the \" instrument \" was also a satire of the audience expectations of piano playing performance , intended to cause discomfort for the audience as well as the ===performer=== . noted an octave higher , the score specifies several different techniques for striking the strings , including the scraping of fingers , using the flat of the hand , and the tapping of the foot .", "replaced_ids": [229, 229], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "double jeopardy is an empirical law in marketing where , with few exceptions , the lower market share brands in a market have both far fewer buyers in a time period and also lower brand loyalty . the term was originally coined by social scientist william mcphee in 1963 who observed the phenomenon , first in ===sales=== and likings for other brands , and then in behaviours ( e . g . reading of comic strips and listening to radio stations ) . soon afterwards , david lewisson formulated the double jeopardy law applied primarily to repeat consumption . subsequently , double jeopardy has been found to apply across products as diverse as laundry detergent to diesel fuel , across space and time . this random law - like phenomenon is due to a statistical interference effect that arises if brands are broadly equally effective in not selling to much of the same types of consumers ( often referred to as a mechanism of product selection and market dominance theory ) . the double jeopardy law generalization is explained and generalized by the von neumann type - theory and the theory of rational choice . see also , in - jones , cohn , and johnson ( 1985 ) .", "replaced_ids": [56, 56], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "tresor is a software approach that seeks to resolve this insecurity by storing and manipulating encryption keys almost exclusively on the cpu alone , and in registers accessible at ring 0 ( the highest privilege level ) only \u2014 the exception being the brief period of initial calculation at the start of a session . this ensures that encryption keys are almost never accessed via user code or during a cold boot attack . tresor is written as a kernel software that stores encryption keys in the same as debug registers , and performs on - the - fly for code generation , compression operations , and elimination of the user code inaccessible to the \" hidden \" register for encryption . tresor was initially widely known only by a 2010 paper by christian johannessen which addressed the cold boot security issue . he concluded that modern x86 processors had two register classes where bit - slice kernel access was realistic : the hidden register registers which could in general be made privileged by an attacker for all sse programs ( and ===thus=== , any program running on them ) , and the debug registers which were much lower but had no such issues . he left the latter for others to examine , and released a proof of concept program called desor , based on the sse register classes . its developers noted that \" using tresor on a 32 - bit cpu that supports aes - ni , there is no performance degradation compared to a modern implementation of aes \" , and run slightly faster than the kernel without the need for code to be generated automatically , a result which has surprised the public as well .", "replaced_ids": [182, 182], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "the bunny hop is executed by approaching an obstacle with a medium rolling speed , arms and legs slightly bent . upon reaching the obstacle , the rider first begins to shift their centre of gravity towards the rear tire of the bike and push back on the front wheel down , causing the front wheel to lift as if doing a hop . as the front wheel reaches chest height , they ' scoop ' up the rear of the bike by snapping their wrist forward and applying backwards and upwards pressure to the front tire , while pushing down and back on the handlebars . it helps to think about the lifting of the back tire as snapping one ' s wrist forward and shifting their weight at the same time . the combination of these two techniques allows the rider to first raise their centre of gravity , and then lift the bike with them , to achieve greater ground clearance . the other technique , more commonly performed on a ===bike=== with full suspension , is applying a low - end compression downwards into bars and pedals , once full compression is achieved then pushes them forward re - applying on both bars and pedals equal amounts so that both front and rear wheels touch the ground . this technique can also be combined with a lowering of the bike through clip less pedals and is sometimes called the english bunny hop .", "replaced_ids": [174, 174], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "an instrument needle valve uses a tapered pin to gradually open a space for fine control of flow . the flow can be controlled and regulated with the use of a small screw . a needle valve has a relatively small orifice with a short , tapered pin , and a needle - threaded screw mounted on the end of a needle , which precisely fits the seat . as the handle is extended and the needle is retracted , movement between the seat and the fluid flow is possible ; however , until the plunger is completely retracted , the fluid flow is significantly impeded . since it takes many twists of the needle - threaded screw to fully reopen the pin area , careful control of the flow rate is not necessary . the name of the needle valve is from the vernier notation of the difference between the needle ' s length and its diameter , or the difference in diameter between lever and needle . a long shift in pressure ( the pump pressure ) allows for a very rapid and complex flow rate , ( affecting the fluid flow ) . needle valves may also be used in vacuum systems , when a careful control of gas flow is needed , at elevated pressures , such as when filling gas - cooled vacuum engines , ===in=== lasers and similar devices .", "replaced_ids": [230, 230], "hallucination": 1}

{"replaced": "in signal processing and related disciplines , aliasing is an effect that causes different signals to become indistinguishable ( or aliases of one another ) when sampled . it also often refers to the distortion or artifact that ===occurs=== when a signal reconstructed from samples is distinguished from the original continuous signal . aliasing can occur in signals sampled in memory , for example digital audio , and is referred to as temporal aliasing . it can also occur in multiple independently sampled signals ( e . g . moire images in digital images ) ; this type of aliasing is called spatial aliasing . spatial alias is best avoided by applying lowpass filtering or anti - echo - filters ( avcs ) to the input signal before sampling and when converting a signal from a higher to a lower sampling rate . additional reconstruction techniques should then be used when restoring the recorded signal to the continuous signal or converting a signal from a lower to a higher sampling rate . for spatial anti - aliasing , the techniques of anti - aliasing include frequency modulation anti - aliasing ( cmi alias ) , optical fiber interference anti - aliasing , and linear transform reconstruction .", "replaced_ids": [38, 38], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "metric search is similarity search which takes place within metric spaces . while the above two properties are more or less necessary for any kind of search to be meaningful , the further property of triangle inequality is required for mathematical , rather than statistical , purposes . a simple corollary of the theorem is that , if any two objects within the set are far apart , then no reference object can be close to both . this property allows metrics to be built , based on distances ===found=== within the data collection , which allow subsets of the data to be sorted when a search is necessary . as a simple example , a reference object can be removed from the data set , and the elements of the set divided into two classes based on distances to this object : those close to the reference object in set a , and those distant from the object in set b . if , when the query is later queried , the distance from the query to the reference object is infinite , then none of the objects within set a can be very close to the query ; if it is very small , then no objects within set b can be close to the query . once such concepts are well understood , and understood , many different metric space data sets can be designed , variously suitable for different types of collections . the general domain of metric search can thus be characterised as the study of pre - linear regression over large and relatively diverse collections of data which , using the properties of metric spaces , enable efficient statistical analyses to be done .", "replaced_ids": [89, 89], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "an expendable launch system ( or expendable launch vehicle / elv ) is a launch vehicle that can be launched only once , after which its components are either destroyed during reentry or discarded in space . elvs typically consist of several rocket stages that are launched from orbit as their fuel is exhausted and the craft gains range and endurance . most satellites and other spacecraft are now based on elvs . elvs are simpler in design than reusable launch systems and therefore may have a lower production rate . furthermore , an aircraft engine can use its own fuel system to accelerate its payload , offering greater fuel efficiency . both concepts are revolutionary technologies in wide - ===scale applications=== for aerospace exploration . these vehicles are launched only once , and therefore have a much lower per - launch cost than reusable vehicles . new commercial orbiter launch systems under development by american companies such as aerospace dynamics and blue origin have the potential to replace many existing launch systems due to the lower per - launch cost of reusable platforms .", "replaced_ids": [120, 121], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "in playing a particular hand of poker , a freeroll is a situation that arises ( usually when only two players remain ) before the last card has been dealt , in which one player is guaranteed to at least split the pot with his opponent no matter what the final cards are , but where there is some chance he can win the whole pot if certain final cards are dealt . this most commonly occurs in a high - low poker hand where the player knows that he has a bad low card made , his opponent cannot make a better low no matter what the last card is , but the player who is wrong might possibly catch a third card that gives him a straight or flush , or both as well . here ' s an example from texas hold ' em : angie holds k\u2663 5\u2665 , and burt held a straight card made . after the fourth card is dealt , the board is a\u2663 3\u2663 j\u2665 k\u2660 . both players have an ace - high straight , the current last hand , and so they will most likely split the pot . but if the final card happens to be a straight , burt ' s straight will lose to angie ' s straight . there is no other such a card that will give burt more than a straight ; only angie can improve , so she is always ahead of burt . if a player knows he has a good hand , he can split the pot with a straight flush , and often a less - experienced player with a good hand who does not ===know=== that he is on the receiving end of the flush , will continue to put in raises with no possible possibility of gain .", "replaced_ids": [286, 286], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "a rogowski coil , named after walter rogowski , is an electrical device for measuring alternating current ( ac ) or high - speed current pulses . it consists of a helical coil of wire with the lead from one end passing through the core of the wire to the other end , so that both ends are at the same end of the coil . the whole assembly is then wrapped around the magnetic field whose strength is to be measured . there is no magnetic ( static ) field . the winding geometry , the diameter of the coil and the magnetic field of the conductor are adjustable for maximum immunity to such fields and low sensitivity to the positioning of the measured current . since the voltage that is ===produced=== in the coil is proportional to the rate of change ( current ) of current in the outer conductor , the output of the rogowski coil is usually coupled to an electrical ( or electronic ) integrator circuit to produce an output voltage that is proportional to the current . single - chip signal processors with built - in analog to digital converters are often used for this purpose .", "replaced_ids": [132, 132], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "in computer graphics , a silhouette edge on a 3d body projected onto a 2d plane ( display plane ) is the collection of points whose outwards surface normal is perpendicular to the view vector . due to the large difference here in the surface normal , a silhouette edge is also an edge which separates a front facing face from a back facing face . without loss of generality , this edge is usually chosen to be the closest one on a plane , so that in this case this edge corresponds to the same one in a real face . hence , if there is an edge between a front facing face and a side facing face , and another edge between a side facing face and back facing face , the nearest one is chosen . the easy example is looking at a face in the plane where the face normal is collinear with the view vector . the second kind of silhouette edge is sometimes troublesome to handle because it does not necessarily correspond to a physical edge in the cad model . the reason that this can be an issue is that a algorithm might improve the original solution by adding the new silhouette edge into the problem . also , given that the solution strongly depends upon the geometry of the model and the vector , this can introduce ===some=== instabilities into the algorithm ( such as when a trick or lack thereof of symmetry is involved ) .", "replaced_ids": [235, 235], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "in compiler design , static single assignment form ( often abbreviated as ssa form or simply ssa ) is a property of an intermediate representation ( ir ) , which requires that each variable is assigned exactly once , and every variable is defined before it is used . the variables in the resulting ir are ===divided=== into distinct , new variables , indicated by the same name with a subscript in brackets , so that every variable has its own value . in this simple form , def - def operations are performed and each contains a unique value . ssa was proposed by richard m . martin , david a . wegman , and f . james whiteford in 1988 . ron cytron , jeanne ferrante and the previous three researchers at ibm invented an algorithm that can compute the ssa form efficiently . one can expect to use ssa in a compiler for java se or c , whereas in other language compilers , such as those for scheme , c and java ee , statement - passing style ( cps ) is widely used . cps is formally equivalent to a well - defined definition of concurrency , excluding global - level control flow , which does not occur when both ir is used as input data . so optimizations and problems arising in support of both ir apply to the other .", "replaced_ids": [56, 56], "hallucination": 0}

{"replaced": "informally , substitute goods \u2013 as contrasted with complementary goods and independent goods \u2013 are goods that , as a result of changed conditions , may replace each other in use ( or consumption ) . the assumption that one good is always a substitute good for another has immediate positive implications : the same way as one good can be substituted for another , the demands for the two goods will be interrelated by the fact that one can trade off one good for the other if it becomes ===necessary enough=== to do so . that is , an increase in the price of a good will ( ceteris paribus ) increase demand for its substitutes . conversely , a decrease in the price of a good will increase demand for its substitutes . more formally , the relation between demand curves determines whether goods are used as substitutes or not substitutes . a substitute good is a good with a positive cross - section of demand . this implies that , if it is a substitute for it , an increase in the price of will result in a leftward movement along the demand curve of and cause the demand curve for to shift out . a decrease in the price of will result in a rightward movement along the demand curve of and cause the demand curve for to shift in .", "replaced_ids": [90, 91], "hallucination": 0}
